Required proof: Fixture first reproduces the old scope failure using real Store epochs and current-read entitlements, without claiming decoded media from that unit test. Unchanged flows must remain authorized while each of the four real writer classes is held; changed connections, identity/conversation revocation, expiry, cancellation, cross-Store races and changing-lifecycle fallback must still stop the correct flows. Media reviews the counter and implementation; Root runs units and then the entire regression cohort, including actual Opus/VP8 programmes and unchanged quality limits.
Fix: Add a distinct connection authority domain and register the original connection dependencies in Native/WebRTC media reads. Keep conversation and identity reads for authorization, while each handoff phase writes only its affected connections and operation records. Cleanup must prove unchanged lifecycle in the same SQL transaction; genuine broader changes retain broad fencing. No lock upgrade under SQL, renewed media age, epoch resurrection or duplicate physical effect is permitted.
State: diagnosing; implementation: Reopened for the remaining physical-commit, public-activation, old-native cleanup and replacement-cleanup write scopes. Whole-conversation and identity write admission permanently revokes healthy media epochs for unchanged connections. A connection-specific footprint is being designed; no production fix or old counter has run yet. Blockers: B191. Dependencies: P1.1.
Owner: /root/v198_resources. Counter tests: /root/fixture_blockers. Reviewer: /root/media_blockers. Coordinator: /root.
Checkpoint: The complete run on 07e41461/411 executed all 241 cases: 239 passed and two full media programmes failed video FPS. All 224 component cases and 15 of 17 workloads passed, including every explicitly enabled RTC lane and the previously failing audio-overlap case. Both programmes completed four moves and four bidirectional 64 KiB Data exchanges, ended both Sessions by 64.56 seconds under the original 67-second cutoff, and observed ten seconds idle with no runtime owners. EdDSA failed three video bins and ES256 failed two, all against the unchanged 24 FPS limit. New diagnostics account exactly for every missing packet on all four affected retained-video flows: Core forwarding, authorization and age-expiry drops precede the packetizer; accepted transport counts equal receiver counts. The next fix targets overbroad invalidation during physical commit, public activation and both native/replacement cleanup paths. Those paths can revoke unchanged participants' media epochs by taking conversation-wide write scopes. Resource owns the scoped-write implementation, Fixture owns causal regressions, Media independently reviews safety and Root coordinates units plus the next complete run. Epochs will not be revived, and quality limits remain unchanged. Packet-reordering work stays unapplied because it does not explain these losses. Shipping and full32 remain blocked; v215 is still the last matrix at 0/32. G6-054 remains parked.
